title: Knowledge check: Importing and Exporting Tabular Data

questions.prompt: Which workflow is most reliable when applying Importing and Exporting Tabular Data?
options: Build from a small, labeled range and compare the actual result with an independently checked expectation.
Assume a visible result must be correct and skip checks.
Change several workbook features at once so the source of an error is unclear.
Delete the source records after producing a summary.
questions.answer_key: Build from a small, labeled range and compare the actual result with an independently checked expectation.
questions.explanation: A small labeled range and an independent expected result help verify importing and exporting tabular data without assuming that the first result is correct.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before relying on Importing and Exporting Tabular Data in another workbook?
options: Only the cell fill color; all workbooks treat inputs and functions identically.
Verify data types, ranges and target-version support, then test a relevant edge or failure case.
Whether the workbook opens once; no boundary tests are useful.
Whether the formula can be shortened, regardless of readability or compatibility.
questions.answer_key: Verify data types, ranges and target-version support, then test a relevant edge or failure case.
questions.explanation: Correct data types, ranges, version support and edge-case checks prevent many spreadsheet errors.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the difference between an automated text check and a verified Excel deliverable?
options: A matching text string proves workbook functionality on every Excel version.
A displayed number is enough to confirm formula correctness.
Keeping no raw data makes results more auditable.
Keep the raw inputs and assumptions clear; document limitations and request human review for a workbook artifact.
questions.answer_key: Keep the raw inputs and assumptions clear; document limitations and request human review for a workbook artifact.
questions.explanation: The current CodeLeaf grader matches submitted text; it does not execute Excel or inspect uploaded workbook files. Actual workbook quality needs separate result checks and review.

status_note: Repository-side answer keys must not be exposed through learner-facing API responses. Question prompts/options may be served without answer_key or explanations before grading.
